new_items.name: Mythical Beast
new_items.summary: A composite creature of legend joins the parts of several animals into one impossible guardian.

new_items.name: Griffin
new_items.summary: A lion-bodied, eagle-headed guardian of ancient legend soars with broad feathered wings.

new_items.name: Phoenix
new_items.summary: A radiant firebird of legend is reborn from the ashes of its own flames.

new_items.name: Kraken
new_items.summary: A colossal sea monster of northern legend drags ships beneath the waves with giant tentacles.

new_items.name: Heracles
new_items.summary: The mightiest Greek hero, son of Zeus, wears a lion-skin hood and carries a heavy olive-wood club.

new_items.name: Nemean Lion
new_items.summary: The invulnerable golden lion of Nemea was the first monster faced in the labours of Heracles.

new_items.name: Hydra
new_items.summary: The many-headed water serpent of Lerna grew two new heads for every one that was cut off.

new_items.name: Perseus
new_items.summary: The Greek hero Perseus used a mirrored shield and winged sandals to defeat the gorgon Medusa.

new_items.name: Theseus
new_items.summary: The Athenian hero Theseus found his way through the labyrinth by following a red thread.

new_items.name: Labyrinth
new_items.summary: The winding maze built by Daedalus at Knossos was designed so that no one could escape the Minotaur.

new_items.name: Daedalus
new_items.summary: The legendary Athenian inventor Daedalus designed the labyrinth and crafted wings of feathers and wax.

new_items.name: Icarus
new_items.summary: Icarus flew too close to the sun on wings of wax and feathers and fell into the sea.

new_items.name: Odysseus
new_items.summary: The clever king of Ithaca outwitted a Cyclops on his ten-year voyage home from Troy.

new_items.name: Trojan War
new_items.summary: A ten-year siege of Troy united Greek kings against a walled city in the most famous war of legend.

new_items.name: Achilles
new_items.summary: The near-invincible Greek warrior Achilles could be wounded only at his heel.

new_items.name: Trojan Horse
new_items.summary: A giant hollow wooden horse hid Greek warriors and was wheeled into Troy as a false gift.

new_items.name: Prometheus
new_items.summary: The Titan Prometheus stole fire from the gods and carried it to humanity in a fennel stalk.

new_items.name: Pandora's Jar
new_items.summary: Pandora's great storage jar released every trouble into the world, leaving only hope inside.

new_items.name: Atlas the Sky-Bearer
new_items.summary: The Titan Atlas was condemned to hold up the heavens on his shoulders for eternity.

new_items.name: Hestia
new_items.summary: The gentle Greek goddess of the hearth tends the central flame of every home and temple.

new_items.name: Helios
new_items.summary: The Titan Helios drives the chariot of the sun across the sky every day.

new_items.name: Eros
new_items.summary: The winged Greek god of desire shoots golden arrows that make mortals fall in love.

new_items.name: Oracle of Delphi
new_items.summary: The priestess of Apollo at Delphi spoke prophecies while seated above rising sacred vapours.

new_items.name: Three Fates
new_items.summary: The three Greek Moirai spin, measure and cut the thread of every mortal life.

new_items.name: River Styx
new_items.summary: The dark river Styx marks the boundary between the world of the living and the Greek underworld.

new_items.name: Charon
new_items.summary: The hooded ferryman Charon poles the souls of the dead across the river Styx for a single coin.

new_items.name: Elysium
new_items.summary: The Elysian Fields are the sunlit paradise where Greek heroes rest after death.

new_items.name: Tartarus
new_items.summary: The deepest abyss beneath the Greek underworld imprisons the defeated Titans behind bronze gates.

new_items.name: Centaur
new_items.summary: A centaur has the upper body of a human joined to the body and legs of a horse.

new_items.name: Siren
new_items.summary: The sirens of Greek legend sang so sweetly that passing sailors steered onto the rocks.

new_items.name: Argo
new_items.summary: The Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts on their quest for the Golden Fleece.

new_items.name: Ambrosia
new_items.summary: Ambrosia is the golden food of the Olympian gods that grants immortality.

new_items.name: Cupid
new_items.summary: The Roman god of love is shown as a winged child aiming his golden arrows.

new_items.name: Aeneas
new_items.summary: The Trojan hero Aeneas escaped burning Troy and became the legendary ancestor of the Romans.

new_items.name: Romulus and Remus
new_items.summary: The twin sons of Mars were raised by a she-wolf and went on to found the city of Rome.

new_items.name: Fortuna
new_items.summary: The Roman goddess of luck turns a great wheel that raises and lowers mortal fortunes.

new_items.name: Sol Invictus
new_items.summary: The Unconquered Sun was honoured by later Romans with a radiant crown of light.

new_items.name: Proserpina
new_items.summary: The Roman queen of the underworld returns to the surface each spring, bringing the flowers with her.

new_items.name: Lares
new_items.summary: The Lares were Roman household guardian spirits honoured at a small shrine in every home.

new_items.name: Cumaean Sibyl
new_items.summary: The prophetess of Cumae wrote her oracles on leaves inside a cave of a hundred openings.

new_items.name: Huginn and Muninn
new_items.summary: Odin's two ravens, Thought and Memory, fly over the world each day and report back to him.

new_items.name: Mimir's Well
new_items.summary: Mimir's well of wisdom lies beneath a root of Yggdrasil, where Odin traded an eye for a drink.

new_items.name: Norns
new_items.summary: The three Norns weave the destinies of gods and humans at the well beneath the world tree.

new_items.name: Nidhogg
new_items.summary: The dragon Nidhogg gnaws at the deepest roots of the world tree Yggdrasil.

new_items.name: Muspelheim
new_items.summary: Muspelheim is the blazing Norse realm of fire, home of the fire giants.

new_items.name: Surtr
new_items.summary: The fire giant Surtr guards Muspelheim with a flaming sword destined to set the world ablaze.

new_items.name: Svartalfheim
new_items.summary: Svartalfheim is the underground Norse realm of master smiths who forged the treasures of the gods.

new_items.name: Draupnir
new_items.summary: Odin's golden ring Draupnir drips eight new rings of equal weight every ninth night.

new_items.name: Brisingamen
new_items.summary: The radiant necklace Brisingamen was forged by dwarven smiths for the goddess Freyja.

new_items.name: Njord
new_items.summary: The Norse god of the sea, wind and fishing is the father of Freyr and Freyja.

new_items.name: Apples of Idunn
new_items.summary: The golden apples kept by the goddess Idunn keep the Norse gods eternally young.

new_items.name: Gjallarhorn
new_items.summary: Heimdall's great horn Gjallarhorn will sound across all realms to announce Ragnarok.

new_items.name: Einherjar
new_items.summary: The Einherjar are the chosen fallen warriors who feast and train in Valhalla until Ragnarok.

new_items.name: Ymir the First Giant
new_items.summary: The primordial giant Ymir was born where the ice of Niflheim met the fire of Muspelheim.

new_items.name: Sigurd
new_items.summary: The Norse hero Sigurd slew the dragon Fafnir with a reforged sword.

new_items.name: Fafnir
new_items.summary: Fafnir was transformed by greed into a great dragon guarding a hoard of cursed gold.

new_items.name: Ankh
new_items.summary: The ankh is the ancient Egyptian hieroglyph for life, carried by gods as a sacred symbol.

new_items.name: Khepri
new_items.summary: The scarab god Khepri rolls the morning sun into the sky each dawn.

new_items.name: Bennu
new_items.summary: The Bennu is the sacred Egyptian heron of creation and renewal, linked to the sun.

new_items.name: Sphinx
new_items.summary: The sphinx joins a lion's body with a human head as a guardian of Egyptian temples and tombs.

new_items.name: Book of the Dead
new_items.summary: The Egyptian Book of the Dead is a papyrus scroll of spells guiding the deceased through the afterlife.

new_items.name: Ma'at
new_items.summary: The Egyptian goddess Ma'at embodies truth, balance and cosmic order, marked by a single ostrich feather.

new_items.name: Weighing of the Heart
new_items.summary: In the Egyptian afterlife a heart is weighed against the feather of Ma'at to judge a life.

new_items.name: Duat
new_items.summary: The Duat is the Egyptian underworld traversed each night by the sun and by the souls of the dead.

new_items.name: Solar Barque
new_items.summary: Ra's sacred boat carries the sun through the sky by day and the Duat by night.

new_items.name: Nut the Sky Goddess
new_items.summary: The Egyptian sky goddess Nut arches her star-covered body over the earth.

new_items.name: Geb
new_items.summary: Geb is the Egyptian god of the earth, often shown reclining green beneath the sky.

new_items.name: Canopic Jars
new_items.summary: Four canopic jars with animal and human-headed lids preserved organs during mummification.

new_items.name: Cuneiform Tablet
new_items.summary: Clay tablets pressed with wedge-shaped cuneiform signs preserve the earliest written stories of Mesopotamia.

new_items.name: Mesopotamian Mythology
new_items.summary: The myths of Sumer, Akkad and Babylon tell of creation, floods and the first heroes between two rivers.

new_items.name: Ziggurat
new_items.summary: A ziggurat is a massive stepped temple tower of mud brick built to bring the gods closer to earth.

new_items.name: Anunnaki
new_items.summary: The Anunnaki are the great assembly of Mesopotamian gods who decree the fates of the land.

new_items.name: Anu
new_items.summary: Anu is the ancient Mesopotamian god of the heavens and father of many gods.

new_items.name: Enki
new_items.summary: Enki, god of wisdom and fresh water, is shown with streams of water and fish flowing from his shoulders.

new_items.name: Inanna
new_items.summary: Inanna, queen of heaven, is the Mesopotamian goddess of love, war and the morning star.

new_items.name: Ereshkigal
new_items.summary: Ereshkigal rules the Mesopotamian underworld, the land of no return.

new_items.name: Babylon
new_items.summary: Babylon was the great Mesopotamian city famed for its glazed gates and towering temple.

new_items.name: Marduk
new_items.summary: Marduk is the patron god of Babylon who defeated the chaos dragon Tiamat.

new_items.name: Tiamat
new_items.summary: Tiamat is the primordial goddess of the salt sea, imagined as a vast chaos serpent.

new_items.name: Lamassu
new_items.summary: The lamassu is a winged bull with a human head that guarded Assyrian palace gates.

new_items.name: Gilgamesh
new_items.summary: Gilgamesh is the legendary king of Uruk whose quest for immortality became the oldest great epic.

new_items.name: Humbaba
new_items.summary: Humbaba is the monstrous guardian of the Cedar Forest slain by Gilgamesh and Enkidu.

new_items.name: Epic of Gilgamesh
new_items.summary: The Epic of Gilgamesh is one of the oldest surviving works of literature, written on clay tablets.

new_items.name: Tablet of Destinies
new_items.summary: The Tablet of Destinies grants whoever holds it supreme authority over the fate of the universe.

new_items.name: Druid
new_items.summary: Druids were the learned priests, judges and keepers of lore among the ancient Celtic peoples.

new_items.name: Celtic Mythology
new_items.summary: The myths of the Irish, Welsh and Gaulish Celts are filled with otherworlds, heroes and shape-shifting gods.

new_items.name: Tuatha De Danann
new_items.summary: The Tuatha De Danann are the divine race of Irish myth who arrived in Ireland wrapped in mist.

new_items.name: The Dagda
new_items.summary: The Dagda is the great father god of Irish myth, master of a club, a harp and a cauldron.

new_items.name: Cauldron of the Dagda
new_items.summary: The Dagda's cauldron of plenty never empties and leaves no one hungry.

new_items.name: Lugh
new_items.summary: Lugh is the radiant Irish god skilled in every art and wielder of an unstoppable spear.

new_items.name: Brigid
new_items.summary: Brigid is the Irish goddess of poetry, healing and the smith's fire.

new_items.name: Morrigan
new_items.summary: The Morrigan is the Irish goddess of fate and battle who appears as a crow over the field.

new_items.name: Cernunnos
new_items.summary: Cernunnos is the antlered Celtic god of wild animals, forests and abundance.

new_items.name: Sidhe Mound
new_items.summary: The sidhe mounds are grassy hills where the Tuatha De Danann withdrew into hidden halls.

new_items.name: Banshee
new_items.summary: The banshee is a spirit woman of the sidhe whose keening wail foretells a death in the family.

new_items.name: Tir na nOg
new_items.summary: Tir na nOg is the Irish otherworld land of eternal youth across the western sea.

new_items.name: Selkie
new_items.summary: Selkies are seal-folk of Celtic and Norse coastal legend who shed their skins to walk on land.

new_items.name: Cu Chulainn
new_items.summary: Cu Chulainn is the great hero of Ulster, son of the god Lugh, who held a ford alone against an army.

new_items.name: Salmon of Knowledge
new_items.summary: The Salmon of Knowledge grants all the world's wisdom to the first person who tastes it.

new_items.name: Ogham Stone
new_items.summary: Ogham stones carry the notched alphabet of early Ireland cut along their edges.

new_items.name: Precambrian Eon
new_items.summary: The Precambrian covers nearly nine-tenths of Earth's history, from its formation to the first complex animals.

new_items.name: Stromatolite
new_items.summary: Stromatolites are layered rock mounds built by microbial mats, among the oldest evidence of life.

new_items.name: Dickinsonia
new_items.summary: Dickinsonia is a flat, ribbed Ediacaran organism and one of the earliest known animals.

new_items.name: Snowball Earth
new_items.summary: During Snowball Earth episodes, ice sheets may have covered almost the entire planet.

new_items.name: Ordovician Period
new_items.summary: The Ordovician seas filled with reefs, giant nautiloids and early jawless fish.

new_items.name: Silurian Period
new_items.summary: In the Silurian, the first small plants colonised the land while sea scorpions ruled the reefs.

new_items.name: Devonian Period
new_items.summary: The Devonian is the Age of Fishes, when armoured fish thrived and the first forests appeared.

new_items.name: Permian Period
new_items.summary: The Permian saw dry inland deserts on a single supercontinent and sail-backed synapsids.

new_items.name: Pangaea
new_items.summary: Pangaea was the supercontinent that joined almost all of Earth's land into one mass.

new_items.name: Gondwana
new_items.summary: Gondwana was the southern supercontinent that split away from Pangaea and later broke into the southern continents.

new_items.name: Chicxulub Impact
new_items.summary: A huge asteroid struck the Yucatan region 66 million years ago, ending the Cretaceous.

new_items.name: Mass Extinction
new_items.summary: A mass extinction wipes out a large share of Earth's species in a geologically short time.

new_items.name: Great Dying
new_items.summary: The end-Permian Great Dying was the worst extinction in Earth's history, erasing most marine species.

new_items.name: Paleogene Period
new_items.summary: The Paleogene followed the dinosaurs' extinction, as mammals and birds rapidly diversified.

new_items.name: Index Fossil
new_items.summary: Index fossils such as trilobites lived for a short, well-known time span and are used to date the rock layers they are found in.

new_items.name: Burgess Shale
new_items.summary: The Burgess Shale is a famous Cambrian fossil bed that preserves even soft-bodied animals.

new_items.name: Hallucigenia
new_items.summary: Hallucigenia was a tiny Cambrian worm-like animal with paired spines on its back and slender legs below.

new_items.name: Opabinia
new_items.summary: Opabinia had five stalked eyes and a long flexible nozzle tipped with a grasping claw.

new_items.name: Pikaia
new_items.summary: Pikaia is a small eel-like Cambrian chordate, an early relative of animals with backbones.

new_items.name: Orthoceras
new_items.summary: Orthoceras was a straight-shelled nautiloid whose cone-shaped fossils are common in Ordovician rocks.

new_items.name: Sea Lily
new_items.summary: Sea lilies, or crinoids, are stalked animals whose fossil stems form whole beds of limestone.

new_items.name: Sea Scorpion
new_items.summary: Eurypterids, or sea scorpions, were large predatory arthropods of Silurian seas.

new_items.name: Cooksonia
new_items.summary: Cooksonia was one of the first land plants, a tiny leafless stem forking into spore-bearing tips.

new_items.name: Archaeopteris
new_items.summary: Archaeopteris was a Devonian tree that formed some of the first forests on Earth.

new_items.name: Tiktaalik
new_items.summary: Tiktaalik was a Devonian fish with sturdy fins and a neck, a step toward four-legged animals.

new_items.name: Coelacanth
new_items.summary: The coelacanth is a lobe-finned fish lineage from the Devonian, rediscovered alive in 1938.

new_items.name: Arthropleura
new_items.summary: Arthropleura was a giant millipede-like arthropod over two metres long in Carboniferous forests.

new_items.name: Scale Tree
new_items.summary: Scale trees like Lepidodendron grew in Carboniferous swamps and their remains formed coal.

new_items.name: Dimetrodon
new_items.summary: Dimetrodon was a sail-backed Permian synapsid, more closely related to mammals than to dinosaurs.

new_items.name: Edaphosaurus
new_items.summary: Edaphosaurus was a plant-eating sail-backed synapsid whose sail spines carried knobby crossbars.

new_items.name: Gorgonops
new_items.summary: Gorgonops was a Permian top predator with long sabre-like canine teeth, long before sabre-toothed cats.

new_items.name: Lystrosaurus
new_items.summary: Lystrosaurus was a stocky tusked mammal relative that survived the Great Dying and spread across Pangaea.

new_items.name: Diplocaulus
new_items.summary: Diplocaulus was a Permian amphibian with a remarkable boomerang-shaped head.

new_items.name: Helicoprion
new_items.summary: Helicoprion was a Permian shark relative with a spiral whorl of teeth in its lower jaw.

new_items.name: Ginkgo
new_items.summary: Ginkgo trees have survived since the age of dinosaurs and still grow today as living fossils.

new_items.name: First Flower
new_items.summary: Early Cretaceous plants such as Archaefructus were among the first flowering plants.

new_items.name: Petrified Wood
new_items.summary: Petrified wood forms when minerals replace a buried tree, turning it to colourful stone.

new_items.name: Eoraptor
new_items.summary: Eoraptor, the 'dawn thief', was one of the earliest known dinosaurs, small and lightly built.

new_items.name: Herrerasaurus
new_items.summary: Herrerasaurus was a large early predatory dinosaur from the Triassic of Argentina.

new_items.name: Coelophysis
new_items.summary: Coelophysis was a slender, fast Triassic theropod known from hundreds of skeletons found together.

new_items.name: Megalosaurus
new_items.summary: Megalosaurus was the first dinosaur ever scientifically named, in 1824, from a fossil jaw.

new_items.name: Majungasaurus
new_items.summary: Majungasaurus was a short-armed abelisaurid from Madagascar with a single knob on its skull.

new_items.name: Yutyrannus
new_items.summary: Yutyrannus was a large early tyrannosaur covered in long filament-like feathers.

new_items.name: Sinosauropteryx
new_items.summary: Sinosauropteryx was the first non-bird dinosaur found with feathers, with a ginger-and-white banded tail.

new_items.name: Troodon
new_items.summary: Troodon was a small, big-eyed feathered dinosaur with one of the largest brains for its size.

new_items.name: Bonebed
new_items.summary: A bonebed is a rock layer packed with the jumbled fossil bones of many animals.

new_items.name: Mapusaurus
new_items.summary: Mapusaurus was a giant South American predator whose bonebed suggests it may have lived in groups.

new_items.name: Patagotitan
new_items.summary: Patagotitan is one of the largest known titanosaurs, with thigh bones taller than a person.

new_items.name: Nigersaurus
new_items.summary: Nigersaurus was a short-necked sauropod with a broad straight-edged mouth packed with hundreds of teeth.

new_items.name: Supersaurus
new_items.summary: Supersaurus was among the longest dinosaurs, a diplodocid with an extremely long neck and tail.

new_items.name: Shunosaurus
new_items.summary: Shunosaurus was a Jurassic sauropod from China with a small spiked club at the end of its tail.

new_items.name: Mussaurus
new_items.summary: Mussaurus, the 'mouse lizard', was first described from tiny hatchlings of an early sauropodomorph.

new_items.name: Ouranosaurus
new_items.summary: Ouranosaurus was an iguanodont herbivore from Africa with a tall sail or hump along its back.

new_items.name: Shantungosaurus
new_items.summary: Shantungosaurus was the largest known hadrosaur, a giant duck-billed plant-eater from China.

new_items.name: Torosaurus
new_items.summary: Torosaurus had one of the largest skulls of any land animal, with a huge frill pierced by two openings.

new_items.name: Kosmoceratops
new_items.summary: Kosmoceratops had the most ornate skull of any ceratopsian, with a fringe of downward-curling hooks.

new_items.name: Einiosaurus
new_items.summary: Einiosaurus was a centrosaurine with a nose horn bent sharply forward like a can opener, known from bonebeds.

new_items.name: Confuciusornis
new_items.summary: Confuciusornis was a toothless early bird from China whose males had two long ribbon tail feathers.

new_items.name: Hesperornis
new_items.summary: Hesperornis was a large flightless diving bird with teeth that hunted fish in Cretaceous seas.

new_items.name: Hatzegopteryx
new_items.summary: Hatzegopteryx was a robust giant azhdarchid pterosaur that was likely the top predator of its island.

new_items.name: Pterodaustro
new_items.summary: Pterodaustro was a pterosaur with an upturned lower jaw of fine bristle-like teeth for filter feeding.

new_items.name: Tylosaurus
new_items.summary: Tylosaurus was a huge mosasaur with a bony, battering-ram snout.

new_items.name: Shonisaurus
new_items.summary: Shonisaurus was a giant Triassic ichthyosaur as long as a bus.

new_items.name: Tanystropheus
new_items.summary: Tanystropheus was a Triassic reptile whose stiff neck was longer than the rest of its body.

new_items.name: Archelon
new_items.summary: Archelon was a giant Cretaceous sea turtle more than four metres long with a leathery shell.

new_items.name: Sarcosuchus
new_items.summary: Sarcosuchus was a giant Cretaceous crocodile relative with a long snout ending in a bulbous tip.

new_items.name: Deinosuchus
new_items.summary: Deinosuchus was a giant alligator relative that ambushed dinosaurs at the water's edge.

new_items.name: Eohippus
new_items.summary: Eohippus, the 'dawn horse', was a dog-sized early horse with several toes on each foot.

new_items.name: Paraceratherium
new_items.summary: Paraceratherium was a hornless giant rhinoceros relative, one of the largest land mammals ever.

new_items.name: Basilosaurus
new_items.summary: Basilosaurus was an early serpent-like whale that was once mistaken for a giant reptile.

new_items.name: Ambulocetus
new_items.summary: Ambulocetus, the 'walking whale', was an early whale that could move on land and in water.

new_items.name: Doedicurus
new_items.summary: Doedicurus was a giant armoured glyptodont with a spiked club at the end of its tail.

new_items.name: Cave Lion
new_items.summary: The cave lion was a large Ice Age cat painted on cave walls by early humans.

new_items.name: Steppe Bison
new_items.summary: The steppe bison was a large long-horned Ice Age bison of the mammoth steppe.

new_items.name: Prehistoric Ape
new_items.summary: Early apes of the Miocene lived in forests and include the ancestors of later great apes and humans.

new_items.name: Gigantopithecus
new_items.summary: Gigantopithecus was a giant ape of Pleistocene Asia, known mostly from huge fossil teeth and jaws.

new_items.name: Australopithecus
new_items.summary: Australopithecus walked upright on two legs, as shown by famous fossil footprints in volcanic ash.

new_items.name: Homo Habilis
new_items.summary: Homo habilis, the 'handy man', is associated with the earliest stone tool industries.

new_items.name: Homo Erectus
new_items.summary: Homo erectus was a tall, long-legged human species that spread across Africa and Asia and used fire.

new_items.name: Neanderthal
new_items.summary: Neanderthals were Ice Age humans of Europe and western Asia, skilled toolmakers and hunters.

new_items.name: Cro-Magnon
new_items.summary: Cro-Magnon is the name for early modern humans of Ice Age Europe, first excavated at a French rock shelter.

new_items.name: Oldowan Chopper
new_items.summary: Oldowan choppers are among the oldest known stone tools, made by knocking flakes from a river cobble.

new_items.name: Stone Hand Axe
new_items.summary: The teardrop-shaped Acheulean hand axe was the all-purpose tool of Homo erectus for over a million years.

new_items.name: Flint Spearhead
new_items.summary: Neanderthals hafted sharp flint points onto wooden shafts to make hunting spears.

new_items.name: Mammoth Hunt
new_items.summary: Ice Age hunters worked together with spears to bring down mammoths for meat, hide and bone.

new_items.name: Mammoth Bone Hut
new_items.summary: Ice Age people built dome-shaped shelters from stacked mammoth bones and tusks covered with hides.

new_items.name: Atlatl
new_items.summary: The atlatl, or spear-thrower, let Ice Age hunters hurl darts much farther and faster.

new_items.name: Ochre Hand Stencil
new_items.summary: Ice Age artists blew red ochre around their hands to leave stencils on cave walls.

new_items.name: Bone Flute
new_items.summary: Flutes carved from bird bone and mammoth ivory are among the oldest known musical instruments.

new_items.name: Lion-Man Figurine
new_items.summary: The Lion-Man is a 40,000-year-old ivory figure combining a human body with a cave lion's head.

new_items.name: Paleontologist
new_items.summary: A paleontologist studies ancient life by finding and interpreting fossils.

new_items.name: Dinosaur Quarry
new_items.summary: A dinosaur quarry is a dig site where fossil bones are exposed layer by layer in the rock.

new_items.name: Plaster Field Jacket
new_items.summary: Fragile fossils are wrapped in plaster-soaked burlap jackets before being carried from the field.

new_items.name: Mounted Skeleton
new_items.summary: A mounted skeleton assembles fossil bones on a frame to show a prehistoric animal standing as in life.

new_items.name: Coprolite
new_items.summary: A coprolite is fossilised dung that reveals what prehistoric animals ate.

new_items.name: Gastrolith
new_items.summary: Gastroliths are polished stomach stones that some dinosaurs swallowed to help grind food.

new_items.name: Fossil Shark Tooth
new_items.summary: Fossil shark teeth are among the most common fossils, shed by the thousands over a shark's life.

new_items.name: Tar Pit
new_items.summary: Asphalt seeps like the La Brea tar pits trapped and preserved thousands of Ice Age animals.

new_items.name: Feather Impression
